title: Which language has the most speakers?
body: Mandarin Chinese has the most native speakers, but English is spoken by the most people in total, as a first or second language.

title: There are more than 7,000 languages
body: About 7,000 languages are spoken in the world. Papua New Guinea has around 840 of them, the most of any country.

title: A flamboyance of flamingos
body: Groups of animals have special names: a flamboyance of flamingos, a murder of crows, a parliament of owls, a pride of lions and a crash of rhinos.

title: A sentence with every letter
body: “The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog” uses all 26 letters of the English alphabet. A sentence like that is called a pangram.

title: Where the word “alphabet” comes from
body: It comes from the first two Greek letters, alpha and beta.

title: Uganda speaks more than 40 languages
body: More than 40 languages are spoken in Uganda. Luganda is the most widely spoken local language, and English and Swahili are official languages.

title: Palindromes read the same backwards
body: Words like “level”, “radar” and “civic” read the same in both directions. So does the sentence “Was it a car or a cat I saw?”.

title: Many English words travelled far
body: English has borrowed words from hundreds of languages: “safari” from Swahili, “pyjamas” from Hindi, “ketchup” from Chinese and “banana” from West African languages.

title: Why we say “Mr” and “Mrs”
body: These are shortened forms of “Mister” and “Mistress”. Writing a shortened form of a word is called an abbreviation.

title: Proverbs: wisdom in a few words
body: Most languages have proverbs. In Swahili people say, “Haba na haba hujaza kibaba”: little by little fills the measure. It teaches that small, steady effort adds up.

title: The longest word in English
body: The longest word in most dictionaries has 45 letters and names a lung disease caused by tiny dust. Few people use it, though!
